newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says no deal to keep Italy out of EMU start.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says no deal to keep Italy out of EMU start.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Wednesday that there had been no secret deal struck to keep Italy out of the starting line-up for European monetary union (EMU).
Asked whether such a plan existed, Waigel told reporters: "There isn't one."
Waigel was speaking after he was questioned on EMU by the German parliament's finance committee, where he said: "All countries that qualify will be able to participate in the first round.
"Otherwise they will be able to participate when they qualify, and no member will be arbitrarily excluded," he said.
Earlier, Italian newspaper Il Sole 24 Ore reported that a deal was taking shape between Bonn and Paris to keep Italy, and with it Spain, out of the first wave of EMU.

Italy and France rejected the report, which quoted sources saying France was coming round to the idea of keeping out Italy and Spain because it feared Germany would otherwise insist on a two-year delay to the currency's planned launch in 1999.
